issues.description: Element: Animal(String) constructor, Animal.getName(), and Animal.setName(). The problem statement (including the UML and the explicit note in problem_statement.md) requires the Animal constructor and the name getter/setter to have protected visibility to enforce the intended encapsulation. The solution implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java declares these three members as public (constructor: public Animal(String name); getter: public String getName(); setter: public void setName(String newName)). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended access level and may lead to inconsistencies between student submissions, tests, and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor and the name accessor methods use protected visibility to match the problem statement and UML. Concretely, change the signatures in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to: 'protected Animal(String name)', 'protected String getName()', and 'protected void setName(String newName)'. Verify and update any solution or test code that relies on public access (adjust access from outside-package callers if any), and leave a comment in the template or instructions if tests expect the protected visibility so students understand the requirement.

issues.description: Concept: the Animal constructor and its name accessor methods. Problem statement (UML and explicit note) specifies a protected constructor and protected getter/setter for the Animal.name attribute (UML uses '#' for the constructor and accessor methods; the textual note at line 88 explicitly requests protected visibility for the getter and setter). In the solution repository, Animal.java declares the constructor Animal(String) and the methods getName() and setName(String) as public (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java lines 6-16). This mismatch between the problem's specified visibility (protected) and the solution's visibility (public) can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and inheritance design and which visibility they should use when implementing the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent with the problem statement: change the Animal constructor and the getName()/setName(String) methods in Animal.java to protected (i.e., 'protected Animal(String name)', 'protected String getName()', 'protected void setName(String)'). Alternatively, if public access was intended, update the problem statement/UML note to accept public visibility for the constructor and accessors. Prefer changing the solution/template code to protected to match the UML and explicit textual requirement.
